subject: Rerank cutover playbook — DataBridge / Redwood implementation plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Rerank cutover playbook — DataBridge / Redwood implementation plan

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together a short operational playbook draft and a few decision points we need to lock before the implementation sprint. Attachment: implementation-mvp.xlsx (mapping + milestone sheet).

High level decisions we need this week:
- Vector store: Redwood-managed hosted vector store vs customer-managed Milvus/Pinecone in GCP.
- Backfill approach: full index seed (one-off) vs incremental rolling backfill during off-peak.
- Rerank evals: golden set size, acceptance criteria (MRR/NDCG targets), and online A/B gating window.

Operational constraints we recommend:
- Backfill window: schedule heavy writes between 02:00–05:00 local (DB) to limit user impact; parallelize by namespace.
- Batch sizing: 5k–50k vectors per job depending on vector size / network.
- KV cache prewarm: populate prefix cache for top 1k queries before cutover.
- Rollback: ability to switch search route to legacy scalar search + cold rerank for 48 hours.

Rerank evaluation guidance (short):
- Offline eval: 200–500 labeled queries (golden set), measure MRR and NDCG@10; target delta >= +6% relative to baseline to proceed.
- Online: 2-week A/B at 5–10% traffic, monitor latency P95 and error rate.

Next steps I propose: sign-off on vector-store choice and pick two dates for a 2-week implementation sprint (seed + eval + cutover). Marissa will own the MAP and scheduling. Karthik will own index schema and backfill scripts.

Can you confirm vector-store preference and whether DataBridge wants Redwood to manage the seed backfill or if you’ll run it in your GCP project?

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

On Fri, May 22, 2026 at 09:12 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samir —
> 
> Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together a short operational playbook draft and a few decision points we need to lock before the implementation sprint. Attachment: implementation-mvp.xlsx (mapping + milestone sheet).

Short answers to your questions and recommended approach: 

- Customer-managed Milvus: yes — we can support customer-managed Milvus behind VPC peering in our Private offering. Notes: we rely on a stable network path for large backfills; we recommend a small temporary increase in network bandwidth for the backfill window. KVS prefix caching is supported but will require a lightweight prewarm job executed from Redwood (we can run it if you prefer).

- Throughput estimates (very rough):
  - Redwood-managed hosted vector store: ~50–120k vectors/min depending on vector size and network (1536-dim will be on the lower end).
  - Customer-managed Milvus (GCP, c3 nodes): ~30–80k vectors/min.
  - For 12M vectors at 50k/min -> ~4 hours of pure indexing; budget for overhead, retries and object fetches -> plan for 8–12 hours in a single-window seed; or run incremental jobs across multiple nights.

- Labeling template: see attached rerank-eval-guidelines.md (fields: query_id, query_text, candidate_id, doc_text_snippet, relevance_label (0–3), notes). Aim for 300 queries with 10–50 judgments each for stable NDCG signals.

Mutual Action Plan (proposed milestones):
1) Kickoff & infra access (Day 0–3) — supply non-prod DB creds, sample data and expected traffic curve. Owner: Samir (DataBridge) / Marissa (Redwood).
2) Schema mapping & small-scale seed (Day 4–7) — Karthik owns schema, run smoke index of 50k vectors in non-prod.
3) Full seed / backfill (Day 8) — choose single-window or rolling; Redwood-run or customer-run decision.
4) Offline rerank eval & A/B config (Day 9–13) — compute MRR/NDCG on golden set; if pass threshold, schedule 2-week A/B.
5) Cutover & monitoring (Day 14–28) — ramp traffic gradually and verify latency SLOs; rollback plan ready.

If DataBridge prefers to run the backfill in GCP, we’ll provide the backfill job (containerized scripts) and a runbook. We can also run it ourselves from Redwood if you’d rather not allocate infra time.

Action items from us today:
- I will upload the labeling template and the MAP to the shared Drive.
- Karthik: can you prepare a short index schema proposal and expected vector size delta by EOD Monday?
- Samir: confirm whether you want Redwood to run the seed backfill or if you’ll run it in your project.

Thanks —
Hannah

Attachment: rerank-eval-guidelines.md

Samir / team — quick technical handoff checklist from CSM/implementation side: 

Technical checklist (short):
- Vector schema: id (string), embedding (float32 array), metadata (json blob: tenant_id, created_at, doc_type, shard_key). Please confirm doc_type values.
- Upsert strategy: use idempotent upserts; backfill job will check existing ids to avoid duplicates.
- Batch parameters: start with 10k vectors per batch; reduce to 5k if network/CU errors spike.
- Shard guidance: keep shards ~10–50M vectors to avoid compaction pauses.
- TTL: none for primary index; consider TTL for ephemeral caches.
- Prewarm: we recommend running a prewarm job to populate top-1k prefix cache before cutover; takes ~30–60 minutes.
- Monitoring: set P95 latency alert at 300ms and error-rate alert at 0.5% during ramp.

Data we need from you now: sample 200 queries + 30 labeled candidates each (or point us at the sample dataset link Samir provided). Non-prod write creds (least-privilege) and expected DB node types.

Scheduling: I have availability next Tue/Wed (May 26/27) for a 45-minute implementation scoping call — recommend invite with devs and infra.

Attachment: rerank-eval-guidelines.md
